implementation_notes: SwiftUI makes the god object the recommended default: a single `final class AppState: ObservableObject` with every piece of screen state, injected into the whole view tree via `@EnvironmentObject`. The framework's injection is doing the reach that `AppState` could otherwise have declared in its initialiser, and every view can therefore mutate every piece of state. Apple's own guidance to pass only what a view needs, and to inject value types rather than the whole environment, is the split. Outside SwiftUI, the same smell appears as a `shared` singleton on `URLSession`-style helpers that quietly accumulate user, cache and auth state.
pitfalls: `@EnvironmentObject` puts the dependency in no initialiser, so the compiler cannot tell you what a view actually uses.
Splitting into several ObservableObjects multiplies the injection points and the invalidation work; that cost is real and is why the smell is often left in place.
`static let shared` on an accumulating helper cannot be reset between previews or tests.
